Reproducing Fedele, Tzovara et al. (2020) from dandiset 000576¶

Paper. Fedele T, Tzovara A, Steiger B, Hilfiker P, Grunwald T, Stieglitz L, Jokeit H, Sarnthein J (2020). The relation between neuronal firing, local field potentials and hemodynamic activity in the human amygdala in response to aversive dynamic visual stimuli. NeuroImage 213, 116705. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2020.116705. The claims file was written from the version of record (main text, legends, Tables 1 and 2, Methods); the supplement was not supplied and carries no finding. The data descriptor of the same recordings (Fedele et al. 2021, Sci Data, doi:10.1038/s41597-020-00790-x) was read for the layout of the data.

Dandiset. DANDI:000576, version 0.231010.1811. The paper (2020) predates the dandiset (2023) and cites no version of it. This is the only published version, so it is pinned; the draft lists the same 27 assets with the same total size.

What the dandiset holds. For each of the 9 patients one session of the video task: the bipolar iEEG of each implanted amygdala (14 channels in all) at 2 kHz as 17 epochs of 26 s, the trial table, and for 5 patients the spike times of 42 sorted units. Each session is deposited twice, as _ecephys.nwb and _ecephys+image.nwb (the second adds a link to the video); the data in each pair are identical (checked below), and each is counted once. The BOLD time courses (clinical fMRI) and the continuous microwire signals (needed for the microwire high gamma power, muHGP) are not in it.

Claim Tested here
fig1b-delta-decrease, fig1c-hgp-increase-first-2s, other-bands-no-effect tested
table2-mi-values, fig1d-delta-hgp-mi-correlation, nsoz-delta-hgp-mi-inverse tested
table2-delta-reduced-12-of-14, table2-hgp-mi-positive-nsoz, fig1e-hgp-not-delta-distinguishes-soz tested
hgp-soz-sensitivity-specificity, fig1f-hgp-more-specific-than-delta tested
neuron-count, fig3a-firing-increase-aversive, fig3a-firing-gradual-sustained tested
fig3b-firing-hgp-no-condition-difference, fig3c-ssi-frv-correlation, fig4b-regression-firing-hgp tested
fig3d-firing-correlations-modalities tested in part (HGP only; muHGP and BOLD are not in the dandiset)
fig3b-firing-muhgp-higher-aversive blocked: the continuous microwire signals are not in the dandiset
fig2-participant4-bold-correlations, table2-bold-correlations-group, table2-bold-correlation-values, bold-hgp-uncorrelated-low-mi, fig4c-regression-firing-bold, fig4d-hgp-bold-covariation blocked: the BOLD time courses are not public

Method details the claims file leaves open are taken from the paper and cited where they are used, here and in the docstring of the helper module amygdala.py.

import time
import warnings
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import yaml
from scipy import stats

import amygdala as A

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

started = time.time()
all_assets = A.assets()
ecephys = sorted([a for a in all_assets if a["path"].endswith("_ecephys.nwb")], key=lambda a: a["path"])
with ThreadPoolExecutor(9) as ex:
    sessions = list(ex.map(A.load_session, ecephys))
print(f"loaded {len(sessions)} sessions from dandiset {A.DANDISET_ID} version {A.DANDISET_VERSION} "
      f"in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

claims = {c["id"]: c for c in yaml.safe_load(claims_file.read_text())["claims"]}

kinds = pd.Series([("video" if a["path"].endswith(".avi") else
                    "ecephys+image.nwb" if a["path"].endswith("+image.nwb") else "ecephys.nwb")
                   for a in all_assets]).value_counts()
print("Assets in the version:", len(all_assets))
print(kinds.to_string())


def same_data(asset):
    """Compare the iEEG, spikes and trials of an `_ecephys+image.nwb` file with its `_ecephys.nwb` twin."""
    twin = next(a for a in ecephys if a["path"] == asset["path"].replace("_ecephys+image.nwb", "_ecephys.nwb"))
    h, g = A.open_asset(twin["asset_id"]), A.open_asset(asset["asset_id"])
    st = lambda f: f["units/spike_times"][:] if "units" in f else np.array([])
    return {"file": asset["path"].split("/")[-1],
            "ieeg_identical": np.array_equal(h["processing/ecephys/LFP/ecephys.ieeg/data"][:],
                                             g["acquisition/ecephys.ieeg/data"][:]),
            "spikes_identical": np.array_equal(st(h), st(g)),
            "trials_identical": np.array_equal(h["intervals/trials/start_time"][:], g["intervals/trials/start_time"][:])}


with ThreadPoolExecutor(9) as ex:
    twins = pd.DataFrame(ex.map(same_data, [a for a in all_assets if a["path"].endswith("+image.nwb")]))
print("\nEach `_ecephys+image.nwb` file against its `_ecephys.nwb` twin:")
print(twins.to_string(index=False))

The 14 bipolar channels are the 14 amygdalae of Table 2 (7 nSOZ, 7 SOZ), and the files' SOZ flags agree with the stars of Table 2. Two ages differ from the paper's Table 1 and from the data descriptor's (subject 2: 39 in the file, 48 in the paper; subject 8: 24 against 27). The location of five channels does not name the amygdala: the right channels of subjects 1, 5 and 9 are labelled "Right Hippocampus, rostral hippocampus", and both of subject 6 "unknown", while the labels (AR, AL), the paper and the data descriptor place every one in the amygdala. The analysis follows the paper and uses all 14.

Every file holds 884000 samples per channel at 0.5 ms (2 kHz), 17 epochs of 26 s. The data are stated in volts, but the values have a standard deviation of tens and reach hundreds to 1546: they are microvolts (the data descriptor's figures are in microvolts). The unit does not enter any result (powers are z-scored, correlations are ranks). The step between consecutive samples at the 16 epoch boundaries is a median 12 to 36 against 1.4 to 1.9 within epochs, above the 99th percentile: the epochs are cut out of the recording and laid end to end, not one continuous trace, although the timestamps run without a gap. Each epoch is therefore filtered on its own (helper).

Every session has 17 trials alternating NEUTRAL and AVERSIVE, 9 and 8, as Methods 4.4 give (eight AVERSIVE and nine NEUTRAL blocks). Trials 2 to 17 start 2 s into their 26 s epoch and last 24 s: the trial table marks the block and leaves out the 2 s baseline clip before it (Methods 4.4, data descriptor Fig. 1a). Trial 1 starts at 0 and lasts 26 s, including its baseline; this is taken as an inconsistency of the table, and block onset is taken at 2 s in every epoch. That the block starts there is consistent with the high gamma and firing responses shown below, which change after 2 s and not before; it is not proven by them.

obs_intervals of every unit: [(17, 0.0, 442.0)]

42 units in 8 amygdalae of 5 patients (1 L and R, 2 L and R, 3 L, 4 L, 7 L and R). Three of these amygdalae (1 R, 2 R, 7 R, 17 units) are SOZ amygdalae in Table 2, while Discussion 3.4 says there were no microwire recordings from SOZ amygdalae; the neuron claims use all units, as the paper's counts (41 neurons) do. Spike times are sorted and lie within 0 to 442 s. Every unit's obs_intervals claims all 17 epochs, but the 16 units of subject 7 have no spike after epoch 11 (the last at 286 s), and 4 units of subject 2 have none in epoch 1, at rates of 2 to 5 Hz elsewhere. These epochs are taken as not recorded for those units (helper, observed_epochs); only the first or last epochs are affected, so each unit's observed epochs are contiguous.

# Do the spikes and the iEEG share a clock? Spike-triggered average of the bipolar channel of the
# unit's own amygdala, against the same with spike times shifted by a random 1 to 5 s.
rng_check = np.random.default_rng(0)
lags = np.arange(-200, 201)            # samples, +-100 ms
sta_rows = []
lfp_of = {(s["subject"], lab): s["lfp"][:, c] for s in sessions for c, lab in enumerate(s["labels"])}
for u in U:
    x = lfp_of[(u["subject"], u["label"])]
    x = (x - x.mean()) / x.std()
    idx = np.round(u["spikes"] * A.FS).astype(int)
    idx = idx[(idx > 400) & (idx < len(x) - 400)]
    sta = x[idx[:, None] + lags].mean(0)
    sh = idx + rng_check.integers(2000, 10000)
    sh = sh[sh < len(x) - 400]
    sta_sh = x[sh[:, None] + lags].mean(0)
    sta_rows.append({"subject": u["subject"], "unit": u["unit"], "peak_abs_sta_within_5ms": np.abs(sta[190:211]).max(),
                     "peak_abs_sta_shifted_within_5ms": np.abs(sta_sh[190:211]).max()})
sta_df = pd.DataFrame(sta_rows)
print(sta_df.groupby("subject")[["peak_abs_sta_within_5ms", "peak_abs_sta_shifted_within_5ms"]].median().round(3).to_string())
print("Units whose STA peak within +-5 ms exceeds the shifted one:",
      int((sta_df.peak_abs_sta_within_5ms > sta_df.peak_abs_sta_shifted_within_5ms).sum()), "of", len(sta_df))
print("Wilcoxon, true against shifted:", stats.wilcoxon(sta_df.peak_abs_sta_within_5ms, sta_df.peak_abs_sta_shifted_within_5ms))

The spike-triggered average of the macro bipolar iEEG within 5 ms of the spike is larger than at shifted spike times in 24 of 42 units (Wilcoxon p = 0.042), with medians by subject from 0.02 to 0.14 SD against 0.02 to 0.06. The lock is weak; the microwires protrude a few millimetres beyond the bipolar contacts, so a weak lock is not evidence of an offset. The shared clock of spikes, iEEG and trial table is consistent with the data (the firing and high gamma responses change at the block onset of the trial table, in the claim sections below) but not shown.

iEEG power: envelopes and the group test¶

Envelopes per band (Methods 4.8) for each of the 14 amygdalae, as the helper computes them. The three readings of "z-scored all data within each trial" that the claims file lists decide the outcomes: trial (over the whole 26 s epoch), baseline (mean and SD of the 2 s baseline clip of the epoch) and amygdala (over all epochs of the amygdala). Two variants are shown beside them and do not enter any count of readings: trialsd (the baseline-corrected envelope divided by its SD within the trial; under trial the baseline correction of Methods 4.8 has no effect, as a constant subtracted before a z-score) and baselinepool (the epoch's baseline mean, with the SD of the baseline clips pooled over all epochs of the amygdala). The second is shown because the SD of baseline rests on 20 samples of a 2 s clip smoothed over 1 s, roughly two independent values, so baseline z-values are noisy; baselinepool shows which baseline results survive a stable SD.

The group test is run over the 24 s block (0 to 24 s from onset, the time base of Fig. 1, "locked to stimulus onset"); the baseline clip is the same in both conditions and follows a block of the other condition. This window is a choice stated here.

In [8]:
HGP_VARIANTS = {"hgp_60_150": (60.0, 150.0), "hgp_60_250": (60.0, 250.0)}   # variants of the open upper edge
t_env = A.times()
block = t_env >= 0
tb = t_env[block]
ENV = {}
for s in sessions:
    for c, lab in enumerate(s["labels"]):
        n = A.table2_number(s["subject"], lab)
        ep = A.epochs(s["lfp"][:, c])
        for band in A.BANDS:
            ENV[(n, band)] = A.envelope(ep, band)
        for name, edges in HGP_VARIANTS.items():
            ENV[(n, name)] = A.envelope(ep, edges)
aversive_of = {s["subject"]: s["aversive"] for s in sessions}
NSOZ = [n for n in range(1, 15) if n not in A.TABLE2_SOZ]
SOZ = sorted(A.TABLE2_SOZ)
ALL = list(range(1, 15))
ZS = ["trial", "baseline", "amygdala"]          # the claims file's readings: these decide outcomes
ZV = ["trialsd", "baselinepool"]                # variants, shown only
ZALL = ZS + ZV
SETS = {"nSOZ": NSOZ, "all14": ALL}


def stack(band, z, amygdalae, base="1s"):
    Y, X, G, L = [], [], [], []
    for n in amygdalae:
        subj = A.TABLE2[n - 1][0]
        y = A.normalise(ENV[(n, band)], z, base)[:, block]
        Y.append(y); X.append(aversive_of[subj].astype(int)); G += [subj] * len(y); L += [n] * len(y)
    return np.vstack(Y), np.concatenate(X), np.array(G), np.array(L)


print("envelopes:", len(ENV), "(14 amygdalae x 6 bands and 2 HGP variants), each", ENV[(1, "delta")].shape, "epochs x samples at",
      A.STEP_S, "s; block samples", block.sum())
# Check of the fast mixed-model t against statsmodels MixedLM at a few time points.
y, x, g, l = stack("delta", "trialsd", ALL)
t_fast, df_fast = A.lmm_t(y, x, g)
cmp = []
for i in [10, 60, 120, 200]:
    d = pd.DataFrame({"power": y[:, i], "condition": x, "patient": g})
    fit = smf.mixedlm("power ~ condition", d, groups=d["patient"]).fit(reml=True)
    cmp.append({"time_s": round(tb[i], 2), "t_fast": round(t_fast[i], 3), "t_mixedlm": round(fit.tvalues["condition"], 3),
                "beta_fast": round(float(np.polyfit(x, y[:, i], 1)[0]), 3), "beta_mixedlm": round(fit.params["condition"], 3)})
print(pd.DataFrame(cmp).to_string(index=False))
# How many independent values the SD of the `baseline` reading rests on: the 2 s clip holds 20 samples
# of an envelope smoothed over 1 s. Lag-1 to lag-10 autocorrelation of the delta and HGP envelopes in the clip:
for band in ["delta", "hgp"]:
    e = np.vstack([ENV[(n, band)][:, ~block] for n in ALL])
    e = e - e.mean(1, keepdims=True)
    ac = [np.mean((e[:, :-k] * e[:, k:]).sum(1) / (e ** 2).sum(1)) for k in (1, 5, 10)]
    print(f"{band}: baseline-clip autocorrelation at 0.1, 0.5, 1 s lag {np.round(ac, 2).tolist()}; "
          f"ratio of the largest to the smallest baseline SD over trials, median over amygdalae "
          f"{np.median([np.ptp(np.log(ENV[(n, band)][:, ~block].std(1))) for n in ALL]):.2f} (natural log)")

The condition effect and its t from the helper's within-patient formula match statsmodels' MixedLM with a random intercept per patient at the time points shown (the small differences in t come from MixedLM's variance estimate when the between-patient variance is near zero). The envelope in the 2 s baseline clip decorrelates within about 0.5 s (autocorrelation 0.03 at 0.5 s), so the SD of the baseline reading rests on a few independent values, and it varies across the trials of one amygdala by a factor of about 6.5 for delta and 4.5 for HGP (median over amygdalae of the ratio of the largest to the smallest); baselinepool replaces it with the SD pooled over the amygdala's baseline clips.

def run_band(band, rng, zs=None):
    """All readings of the group test for one band: z-scoring x amygdala set x cluster statistic, for
    the mixed model and the unpaired t-test variant."""
    rows = []
    for z in (zs or ZALL):
        for set_name, amys in SETS.items():
            y, x, g, l = stack(band, z, amys)
            diff = y[x == 1].mean() - y[x == 0].mean()
            for model in ("lmm", "ttest"):
                pg = g if model == "lmm" else np.zeros(len(g), int)
                for stat in ("mass", "size"):
                    _, df, res = A.cluster_test(y, x, g, rng, model=model, stat=stat, perm_groups=pg,
                                                linked=l if model == "lmm" else None)
                    sig = [r for r in res if r["p"] < 0.05]
                    rows.append({"band": band, "z": z, "reading": "claims" if z in ZS else "variant",
                                 "set": set_name, "model": model, "stat": stat,
                                 "block_mean_A_minus_N": round(diff, 3),
                                 "sig_clusters": "; ".join(f"{'A>N' if r['sign'] > 0 else 'A<N'} {tb[r['start']] - 0.05:.1f} to {tb[r['stop'] - 1] + 0.05:.1f} s p={r['p']:.3f}" for r in sig) or "none",
                                 "n_sig_neg": sum(r["sign"] < 0 for r in sig), "n_sig_pos": sum(r["sign"] > 0 for r in sig),
                                 "s_neg": round(sum((r["stop"] - r["start"]) * A.STEP_S for r in sig if r["sign"] < 0), 1),
                                 "s_pos": round(sum((r["stop"] - r["start"]) * A.STEP_S for r in sig if r["sign"] > 0), 1),
                                 "first_pos_start": min([tb[r["start"]] - 0.05 for r in sig if r["sign"] > 0], default=np.nan),
                                 "smallest_p": round(min([r["p"] for r in res], default=1.0), 3),
                                 "clusters": res})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


SHOW = ["band", "z", "reading", "set", "model", "stat", "block_mean_A_minus_N", "n_sig_neg", "n_sig_pos", "s_neg", "s_pos", "smallest_p", "sig_clusters"]

fig1b-delta-decrease¶

In amygdalae outside the SOZ, delta power (1-4 Hz) is lower during AVERSIVE than during NEUTRAL sequences, and the reduction lasts through the AVERSIVE sequence.

Criterion: under the mixed model, at least one cluster with AVERSIVE below NEUTRAL at permutation p < 0.05 and the AVERSIVE block mean below the NEUTRAL one, under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree; partially reproduced when the clusters cover less than half of the 24 s block.

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The readings of the claims file disagree, as the criterion foresees: the claim holds in 6 of the 12 mixed-model readings. With the z-score over the whole trial (trial) no reading finds a delta cluster, in either amygdala set (smallest cluster p 0.88 and 1.0). With baseline z-scoring AVERSIVE is below NEUTRAL in the 7 nSOZ amygdalae (significant clusters covering 14.3 s of the block) and in all 14 (15.6 s). With amygdala z-scoring the 14 amygdalae give 17.1 s and the 7 nSOZ amygdalae none (smallest p 0.072). The block mean of AVERSIVE minus NEUTRAL is negative under every reading (-0.03 to -1.39). Where clusters are found they cover 14 to 17 s of the 24 s block, against the abstract's "up to 18 s". The variants agree with baseline: baselinepool 13.3 s (nSOZ) and 16.8 s (all 14), trialsd 7.0 s and 16.1 s. The unpaired t-test variant gives the same pattern.

for ax, (set_name, amys) in zip(axes, SETS.items()):
    for z, col in zip(ZALL, ["k", "C0", "C1", "C2", "C3"]):
        y, x, g, l = stack("hgp", z, amys)
        tt, df = A.lmm_t(y, x, g)
        ax.plot(tb, tt, color=col, label=z, ls="-" if z in ZS else ":")
    ax.axhline(stats.t.ppf(0.975, df), color="grey", ls="--", lw=0.8)
    ax.axhline(-stats.t.ppf(0.975, df), color="grey", ls="--", lw=0.8)
    ax.axvline(2, color="r", lw=0.5)
    ax.set_title(f"HGP, {set_name}: mixed-model t, AVERSIVE vs NEUTRAL")
    ax.set_xlabel("time from block onset (s)")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()

All plotted t values are inside the axes (autoscaled).

Result: not reproduced. None of the 12 mixed-model readings and none of the 12 unpaired t-test readings of the claims file finds a significant HGP cluster, in the first 2 s or later, and neither do the two z-scoring variants. The largest mixed-model t in the first 2 s is 3.01, at 0.95 s after onset (baseline, nSOZ), above the cluster-forming threshold at 13 points, and that cluster's permutation p is 0.062 (smallest of the readings 0.056). With the band limited to 60-150 or 60-250 Hz (variants) the only significant HGP clusters are AVERSIVE above NEUTRAL from about 6 to 8 s (baseline, nSOZ, p 0.020 and 0.042) and, with baselinepool, 3.1 to 4.7 s, not in the first 2 s.

Per-amygdala time courses and the other baselines of Methods 4.8¶

Each amygdala's AVERSIVE minus NEUTRAL difference in 2 s bins of the block, for delta and HGP under the three z-scorings of the claims file, to compare with the group curves of Fig. 1B and 1C. Then the two other baselines Methods 4.8 say were tested ("taking as baseline the mean of all epochs, or the mean of the previous epoch. Results remained quantitatively similar"), which the claims file lists as variants. Both subtract one constant per trial, which a z-score over the trial (trial) or over the baseline clip (baseline) removes, so they can change only amygdala and the variants. All are run, mixed model with cluster mass.

            yv = A.normalise(ENV[(n, band)], z)[:, block]
            av = aversive_of[A.TABLE2[n - 1][0]]
            dif = yv[av].mean(0) - yv[~av].mean(0)
            rows.append({"amygdala": n, "soz": n in A.TABLE2_SOZ,
                         **{f"{a}-{a + 2}": round(float(dif[(tb >= a) & (tb < a + 2)].mean()), 2) for a in edges2[:-1]}})
        tab = pd.DataFrame(rows)

rng_b = np.random.default_rng(120)
rows = []
for band in ["delta", "hgp"]:
    for base in ["1s", "allepochs", "prevepoch"]:
        for z in ZALL:
            for set_name, amys in SETS.items():
                y, x, g, l = stack(band, z, amys, base)
                _, _, res = A.cluster_test(y, x, g, rng_b, model="lmm", stat="mass", perm_groups=g, linked=l)
                sig = [r for r in res if r["p"] < 0.05]
                rows.append({"band": band, "baseline": base, "z": z, "set": set_name,
                             "block_mean_A_minus_N": round(float(y[x == 1].mean() - y[x == 0].mean()), 3),
                             "smallest_p": round(min([r["p"] for r in res], default=1.0), 3),
                             "sig_clusters": "; ".join(f"{'A>N' if r['sign'] > 0 else 'A<N'} {tb[r['start']] - 0.05:.1f} to {tb[r['stop'] - 1] + 0.05:.1f} s p={r['p']:.3f}" for r in sig) or "none"})
rb = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("\nBaselines of Methods 4.8 (mixed model, cluster mass):")
print(rb.to_string(index=False))

The per-amygdala tables show no amygdala whose HGP rises in the first 2 s under every z-scoring: under baseline 4 of the 7 nSOZ amygdalae have a positive 0 to 2 s bin, under amygdala 5 and under trial 4, against 0 to 4 of the 7 SOZ amygdalae. The delta difference is negative over the block in 10 to 12 of 14 amygdalae. The baselines of Methods 4.8 leave trial and baseline unchanged, as they must. Under amygdala the mean of all epochs gives delta clusters of 1.6 s (nSOZ) and 4.2 s (all 14) and HGP clusters from 3.2 s; the previous epoch gives delta clusters over most of the block in both sets and an HGP cluster in the nSOZ amygdalae from 0.6 to 5.5 s (p = 0.002). With the trialsd variant two more HGP clusters begin in the first 2 s, both in the nSOZ amygdalae: 0.6 to 1.9 s with the mean of all epochs (p = 0.028) and 0.5 to 8.4 s with the previous epoch (p = 0.002). These three are the only readings here with an HGP cluster that begins in the first 2 s, and all use a baseline other than the 1 s clip. As the blocks alternate, the previous epoch is always a block of the other condition, so this baseline adds the neighbouring block's condition difference to every trial; it is a variant of the claims file and does not change the outcomes above, but the results are not "quantitatively similar" across these baselines here.

other-bands-no-effect¶

No AVERSIVE against NEUTRAL difference is found in the theta, alpha, beta and gamma (30-60 Hz) bands.

A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test (mixed model, cluster permutation, p < 0.05), under the three z-scorings of the claims file and both amygdala sets; the two z-scoring variants are shown.

for band in ["theta", "alpha", "beta", "gamma"]:
    G[band] = run_band(band, np.random.default_rng(103 + list(A.BANDS).index(band)))
ob = pd.concat([G[b] for b in ["theta", "alpha", "beta", "gamma"]])
print(ob[ob.model == "lmm"][SHOW].to_string(index=False))
lm = ob[(ob.model == "lmm") & (ob.stat == "mass")]
print("\nMixed model, cluster mass: bands with any significant cluster, by reading")
print(lm.assign(any_sig=(lm.n_sig_neg + lm.n_sig_pos) > 0).pivot_table(index="z", columns="set", values="any_sig", aggfunc="sum").to_string())
lmall = ob[ob.model == "lmm"].assign(any_sig=lambda v: (v.n_sig_neg + v.n_sig_pos) > 0)
dl_ = G["delta"][G["delta"].model == "lmm"].set_index(["z", "set", "stat"])
by_reading = lmall.groupby(["z", "set", "stat"]).any_sig.any().to_frame("other_band_cluster")
by_reading["delta_effect"] = [(dl_.loc[k].n_sig_neg > 0) and (dl_.loc[k].block_mean_A_minus_N < 0) for k in by_reading.index]
print("\nPer mixed-model reading: does another band have a significant cluster, and does delta show the effect of Fig. 1B?")
print(by_reading.to_string())
cl = by_reading.loc[ZS]
print("Readings of the claims file with no cluster in any other band:", int((~cl.other_band_cluster).sum()), "of", len(cl),
      "; of those, readings with the delta effect:", int((~cl.other_band_cluster & cl.delta_effect).sum()))
print("Readings of the claims file with the delta effect:", int(cl.delta_effect.sum()), "; of those with another band clean:",
      int((cl.delta_effect & ~cl.other_band_cluster).sum()))

Result: not reproduced (resting on an assumption). The readings of the claims file disagree: under trial z-scoring no band has a cluster, while under baseline the mixed model finds clusters with AVERSIVE below NEUTRAL in alpha in the 7 nSOZ amygdalae (13.3 to 15.9 s, p 0.016) and in theta and alpha in all 14 (p 0.002 to 0.028), and under amygdala all four bands have clusters in all 14 amygdalae (none in the 7 nSOZ). The outcome rests on one assumption: the paper's pipeline is one under which its own delta result of Fig. 1B appears, since the paper reports both from the same analysis. Every reading of the claims file that shows the delta effect (baseline in both sets, amygdala in all 14; 6 of 12) also shows a cluster in another band, and the trial reading, the only one with no other-band cluster, shows no delta effect either. Of the variants, baselinepool in the 7 nSOZ amygdalae shows the delta effect and no other-band cluster (the alpha cluster of baseline does not survive a pooled baseline SD); in all 14 it has theta and alpha clusters.

Modulation indices (table2-mi-values and the claims built on them)¶

MI = AVERSIVE minus NEUTRAL time-averaged power over the window where the conditions differ (Methods 4.11, Table 2 legend), per amygdala. Window readings: (a) the group clusters of the band (Fig. 1B and 1C) under the same z-scoring, from the mixed model with cluster mass over the 7 nSOZ amygdalae (a_nSOZ) or all 14 (a_all14); (b) clusters found per amygdala (unpaired t-test of its 8 AVERSIVE against 9 NEUTRAL trials, cluster mass, 500 permutations); and (c), a reading the Results' text gives, fixed windows: "the temporal window of task-dependent modulation, which occurred at stimulus onset in HGP and was sustained throughout the trial in DELTA" (Results 2.1, paragraph 2) and "HGP enhancement in the first 2 s or sustained delta decrease" (Methods 4.11), read as 0 to 2 s for HGP and 0 to 24 s for delta. (a) and (b) are the claims file's readings; (c) is taken from the paper's text as step 1.6 of the protocol allows, and is labelled so in every table.

Where a reading gives no significant window (no group cluster under (a), no cluster in that amygdala under (b)), the MI is left undefined: the paper defines no MI without a window, and Table 2 prints a non-zero MI for each of the 14 amygdalae. A claim is judged only on readings that define every MI it needs; the number of amygdalae each reading defines is printed.

In [17]:
rng_mi = np.random.default_rng(201)


def group_mask(band, z, set_name):
    g = G[band]
    r = g[(g.z == z) & (g.set == set_name) & (g.model == "lmm") & (g.stat == "mass")].iloc[0]
    m = np.zeros(block.sum(), bool)
    for c in r["clusters"]:
        if c["p"] < 0.05:
            m[c["start"]:c["stop"]] = True
    return m


per_amy_cache = {}


def per_amygdala_mask(n, band, z):
    key = (n, band, z)
    if key not in per_amy_cache:
        y = A.normalise(ENV[(n, band)], z)[:, block]
        x = aversive_of[A.TABLE2[n - 1][0]].astype(int)
        _, _, res = A.cluster_test(y, x, np.zeros(len(x), int), rng_mi, model="ttest", stat="mass")
        m = np.zeros(block.sum(), bool)
        for c in res:
            if c["p"] < 0.05:
                m[c["start"]:c["stop"]] = True
        per_amy_cache[key] = m
    return per_amy_cache[key]


def mi(n, band, z, window):
    y = A.normalise(ENV[(n, band)], z)[:, block]
    x = aversive_of[A.TABLE2[n - 1][0]]
    if window.startswith("a_"):
        m = group_mask(band, z, "nSOZ" if window == "a_nSOZ" else "all14")
    elif window == "b":
        m = per_amygdala_mask(n, band, z)
    else:
        m = tb < 2 if band == "hgp" else np.ones(block.sum(), bool)
    if not m.any():
        return np.nan
    return y[x][:, m].mean() - y[~x][:, m].mean()


WINDOWS = ["a_nSOZ", "a_all14", "b", "c"]
MI = pd.DataFrame([{"amygdala": n, "z": z, "window": w, "delta": mi(n, "delta", z, w), "hgp": mi(n, "hgp", z, w)}
                   for n in ALL for z in ZALL for w in WINDOWS])
exp = claims["table2-mi-values"]["expected"]
printed = pd.DataFrame({"amygdala": ALL, "delta_paper": [e["value"] for e in exp[0::2]],
                        "hgp_paper": [e["value"] for e in exp[1::2]],
                        "delta_tol": [e["tolerance"] for e in exp[0::2]], "hgp_tol": [e["tolerance"] for e in exp[1::2]]})
MI = MI.merge(printed, on="amygdala")
MI["soz"] = MI.amygdala.isin(A.TABLE2_SOZ)
MI["delta_ok"] = (MI.delta - MI.delta_paper).abs() <= MI.delta_tol
MI["hgp_ok"] = (MI.hgp - MI.hgp_paper).abs() <= MI.hgp_tol
MI["delta_sign_ok"] = np.sign(MI.delta) == np.sign(MI.delta_paper)
MI["hgp_sign_ok"] = np.sign(MI.hgp) == np.sign(MI.hgp_paper)
summary = MI.groupby(["z", "window"]).agg(within_tol=("delta_ok", "sum"), hgp_within=("hgp_ok", "sum"),
                                          delta_sign=("delta_sign_ok", "sum"), hgp_sign=("hgp_sign_ok", "sum"),
                                          delta_defined=("delta", lambda v: int(v.notna().sum())),
                                          hgp_defined=("hgp", lambda v: int(v.notna().sum())))
summary["values_within_tol_of_28"] = summary.within_tol + summary.hgp_within
summary["signs_agree_of_28"] = summary.delta_sign + summary.hgp_sign
summary["reading"] = ["claims" if z in ZS and w != "c" else "claims z, window from text" if z in ZS else "variant"
                      for z, w in summary.index]
print(summary[["reading", "values_within_tol_of_28", "signs_agree_of_28", "delta_defined", "hgp_defined"]].to_string())
print("\nPer amygdala under the fixed windows (c), every z-scoring, with Table 2:")

Result: not reproduced. No reading gives all 28 values within tolerance: at best 4 of 28 among the claims file's z-scorings (amygdala, window c; 6 with the trialsd variant). No reading gives the 28 signs of Table 2: at best 23 of 28 (amygdala, window c). Window (a) defines no HGP MI, as there is no HGP group cluster, and window (b) defines only 1 to 3 MIs per band.

Does the dandiset's patient numbering match the paper's?¶

Two hints that it may not: the units are in subjects 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 while Table 1 lists MUA for 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 R and 8 L, and subject 2's file gives age 39, the age Table 1 gives for patient 7 (both are gliosis cases with AL, AR implanted and AR in the SOZ, so they could be exchanged without the SOZ flags showing it). The MIs are compared with Table 2 under the file numbering and under two re-mappings: subjects 2 and 7 swapped (amygdalae 3 and 4 against 10 and 11), and subject 7's amygdalae taken as patients 8 L and 5 R (10 against 12, 11 against 7).

        "subject 7 as 8 L and 5 R": {10: 12, 12: 10, 11: 7, 7: 11}}
rows = []
for name, sw in MAPS.items():
    target = [sw.get(n, n) for n in ALL]
    pdl = printed.set_index("amygdala").loc[target]
    for z in ZALL:
        m = MI[(MI.z == z) & (MI.window == "c")].sort_values("amygdala")
        dl, hg = m.delta.values, m.hgp.values
        rows.append({"mapping": name, "z": z, "window": "c",
                     "delta_sign_agree": int((np.sign(dl) == np.sign(pdl.delta_paper.values)).sum()),
                     "hgp_sign_agree": int((np.sign(hg) == np.sign(pdl.hgp_paper.values)).sum()),
                     "within_tol_of_28": int((np.abs(dl - pdl.delta_paper.values) <= pdl.delta_tol.values).sum()
                                             + (np.abs(hg - pdl.hgp_paper.values) <= pdl.hgp_tol.values).sum()),
                     "spearman_delta_vs_table2": round(stats.spearmanr(dl, pdl.delta_paper.values).statistic, 2),
                     "spearman_hgp_vs_table2": round(stats.spearmanr(hg, pdl.hgp_paper.values).statistic, 2)})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

Neither re-mapping brings the MIs clearly closer to Table 2. Under window c and the claims file's z-scorings the signs agree in 16, 19 and 23 of 28 under the file numbering, 20, 21 and 23 with subjects 2 and 7 swapped, and 18, 19 and 23 with subject 7 as patients 8 L and 5 R; the values within tolerance stay at 0 to 4 of 28. The analysis keeps the file numbering, which the SOZ flags, sexes, pathologies and implanted sides of the files support (Table 1).

Claims on the MI values¶

Each claim below is computed under every z-scoring and window. A row counts towards the outcome when its z-scoring is one of the claims file's (trial, baseline, amygdala) and it defines every MI the claim needs; rows of the variant z-scorings and rows with undefined MIs are shown and marked. Window (a) defines no HGP MI (there is no HGP group cluster), and window (b) defines only the 1 to 3 amygdalae per band that have a cluster of their own, so most claims rest on window (c). The printed Table 2 values are run through the same computations as a reference.

In [19]:
soz_mask = np.array([n in A.TABLE2_SOZ for n in ALL])
paper_delta, paper_hgp = printed.delta_paper.values, printed.hgp_paper.values


def readings(need=("delta", "hgp"), amys=None):
    """(z, window, kind, delta MI, HGP MI, defined) for every reading; `defined` when every MI in
    `need` is defined for the amygdalae `amys` (boolean mask over the 14, default all)."""
    sel = np.ones(14, bool) if amys is None else amys
    for z in ZALL:
        for w in WINDOWS:
            m = MI[(MI.z == z) & (MI.window == w)].sort_values("amygdala")
            dl, hg = m.delta.values, m.hgp.values
            ok = all(np.isfinite({"delta": dl, "hgp": hg}[b][sel]).all() for b in need)
            kind = "variant" if z in ZV else "claims"
            yield z, w, kind, dl, hg, ok


def counted(df):
    """Rows that decide the outcome: claims-file z-scoring and every needed MI defined."""
    return df[(df.kind == "claims") & df.defined]

fig1d-delta-hgp-mi-correlation¶

Across the 14 amygdalae, the DELTA modulation index and the HGP modulation index are negatively correlated.

Criterion: Spearman r within 0.067 of -0.67 and p < 0.05 under every reading; partially reproduced when r is negative with p < 0.05 but outside tolerance.

    r = stats.spearmanr(dl, hg) if ok else (np.nan, np.nan)
    rows.append({"z": z, "window": w, "kind": kind, "defined": ok, "r": r[0], "p": r[1]})
rows.append({"z": "Table 2 printed", "window": "", "kind": "paper", "defined": True,
             **dict(zip(["r", "p"], stats.spearmanr(paper_delta, paper_hgp)))})

r1d["within_tol"] = (r1d.r + 0.67).abs() <= 0.067

      f"{int((c.within_tol & (c.p < 0.05)).sum())}; negative with p < 0.05: {int(((c.r < 0) & (c.p < 0.05)).sum())}")

table2-hgp-mi-positive-nsoz¶

All 7 amygdalae outside the SOZ have a positive HGP MI, while the response is absent in amygdalae within the SOZ (6 of 7 negative).

Criterion: both counts match (7 of 7, 6 of 7) and the difference has p < 0.05 under one of the tests: (a) Wilcoxon rank-sum, (b) unpaired t-test, (c) Fisher's exact test of the counts of positive MI (chi-square shown beside it).

In [23]:
rows = []
for z, w, kind, dl, hg, ok in list(readings(need=("hgp",))) + [("Table 2 printed", "", "paper", paper_delta, paper_hgp, True)]:
    if not ok:
        rows.append({"z": z, "window": w, "kind": kind, "defined": ok, "hgp_defined": int(np.isfinite(hg).sum())})
        continue
    pos_n, neg_s = int((hg[~soz_mask] > 0).sum()), int((hg[soz_mask] < 0).sum())
    table = [[pos_n, 7 - pos_n], [int((hg[soz_mask] > 0).sum()), 7 - int((hg[soz_mask] > 0).sum())]]
    rows.append({"z": z, "window": w, "kind": kind, "defined": ok, "hgp_defined": 14, "nSOZ_positive": pos_n, "SOZ_negative": neg_s,
                 "p_ranksum": stats.ranksums(hg[~soz_mask], hg[soz_mask]).pvalue,
                 "p_ttest": stats.ttest_ind(hg[~soz_mask], hg[soz_mask]).pvalue,
                 "p_fisher": stats.fisher_exact(table).pvalue,
                 "p_chi2": stats.chi2_contingency(table, correction=False)[1] if min(map(sum, table)) > 0 and min(map(sum, zip(*table))) > 0 else np.nan})
rh = pd.DataFrame(rows)
rh["counts_match"] = (rh.nSOZ_positive == 7) & (rh.SOZ_negative == 6)
print(rh.round(4).to_string(index=False))
c = counted(rh)
print("Counted readings:", len(c), "; with both counts matching:", int(c.counts_match.sum()))

fig1e-hgp-not-delta-distinguishes-soz¶

The HGP MI, but not the DELTA MI, distinguishes amygdalae within the SOZ from those outside it.

Criterion: under a test, (a) Wilcoxon rank-sum or (b) unpaired t-test, uncorrected, HGP MI differs between nSOZ and SOZ with p < 0.05 and DELTA MI does not; not reproduced when HGP does not differ or DELTA does under every test reading; blocked when the test readings disagree.

In [24]:
rows = []
for z, w, kind, dl, hg, ok in list(readings()) + [("Table 2 printed", "", "paper", paper_delta, paper_hgp, True)]:
    for test, fn in [("ranksum", lambda a, b: stats.ranksums(a, b).pvalue), ("ttest", lambda a, b: stats.ttest_ind(a, b).pvalue)]:
        if not ok:
            rows.append({"z": z, "window": w, "kind": kind, "defined": ok, "test": test})
            continue
        ph, pdl = fn(hg[~soz_mask], hg[soz_mask]), fn(dl[~soz_mask], dl[soz_mask])
        rows.append({"z": z, "window": w, "kind": kind, "defined": ok, "test": test, "p_hgp": ph, "p_delta": pdl,
                     "hgp_nSOZ_minus_SOZ": np.mean(hg[~soz_mask]) - np.mean(hg[soz_mask]),
                     "delta_nSOZ_minus_SOZ": np.mean(dl[~soz_mask]) - np.mean(dl[soz_mask]),
                     "holds": ph < 0.05 and pdl >= 0.05})
re_ = pd.DataFrame(rows)

hgp-soz-sensitivity-specificity¶

HGP enhancement indicates amygdalar functional integrity (outside the SOZ) with sensitivity 7/7 (100%), specificity 6/7 (86%) and accuracy 13/14 (93%).

Criterion: the effect is a positive HGP MI; counts must match; Clopper-Pearson 95% intervals.

In [25]:
rows = []
for z, w, kind, dl, hg, ok in list(readings(need=("hgp",))) + [("Table 2 printed", "", "paper", paper_delta, paper_hgp, True)]:
    if not ok:
        rows.append({"z": z, "window": w, "kind": kind, "defined": ok})
        continue
    tp, fn_ = int((hg[~soz_mask] > 0).sum()), int((hg[~soz_mask] <= 0).sum())
    fp, tn = int((hg[soz_mask] > 0).sum()), int((hg[soz_mask] <= 0).sum())
    rows.append({"z": z, "window": w, "kind": kind, "defined": ok, "TP": tp, "FN": fn_, "FP": fp, "TN": tn,
                 "sensitivity": f"{tp}/7", "specificity": f"{tn}/7", "accuracy": f"{tp + tn}/14",
                 "CI_sens": tuple(round(100 * v) for v in A.clopper_pearson(tp, 7)),
                 "CI_spec": tuple(round(100 * v) for v in A.clopper_pearson(tn, 7)),
                 "CI_acc": tuple(round(100 * v) for v in A.clopper_pearson(tp + tn, 14))})
rs = pd.DataFrame(rows)
rs["counts_match"] = (rs.TP == 7) & (rs.TN == 6)
print(rs.to_string(index=False))
c = counted(rs)
print("Counted readings:", len(c), "; with the counts matching:", int(c.counts_match.sum()))
print("Paper: 7/7 CI [66-100], 6/7 CI [42-99], 13/14 CI [66-99]")
# Other binomial intervals, to see which one the printed bounds follow.
from statsmodels.stats.proportion import proportion_confint
for k, n_ in [(7, 7), (6, 7), (13, 14)]:
    cp1 = (stats.beta.ppf(0.05, k, n_ - k + 1) if k > 0 else 0.0, stats.beta.ppf(0.95, k + 1, n_ - k) if k < n_ else 1.0)
    print(f"{k}/{n_}: two-sided Clopper-Pearson {tuple(round(100 * v) for v in A.clopper_pearson(k, n_))}; "
          f"one-sided 95% bounds {tuple(round(100 * v) for v in cp1)}; Wilson {tuple(round(100 * v) for v in proportion_confint(k, n_, method='wilson'))}; "

Result: not reproduced. Window c gives sensitivity 4/7, 4/7 and 5/7, specificity 3/7, 5/7 and 7/7, accuracy 7/14, 9/14 and 12/14 (trial, baseline, amygdala); none gives 7/7, 6/7 and 13/14. The two-sided Clopper-Pearson intervals of the paper's counts (last row) are 59-100, 42-100 and 66-100%, against the printed 66-100, 42-99 and 66-99%. No single interval method gives all three printed intervals: the one-sided 95% bound gives 65 for 7/7, Wilson gives 65-100, 49-97 and 69-99.

This outcome rests on an assumption: window (c), fixed windows taken from the Results' text, is the only window that defines the MIs it needs, while the paper defines the MI over the interval where the two curves are significantly separated (Table 2 legend). The question is for the authors (methods_unavailable).

fig1f-hgp-more-specific-than-delta¶

The HGP response is more specific than the DELTA response for indicating amygdalar dysfunction within the SOZ, by a chi-square test that is not significant (p about 0.2).

Criterion: reading (a), over the 7 SOZ amygdalae, HGP effect absent (HGP MI not positive) against DELTA effect absent (DELTA MI not negative), chi-square of the 2 x 2 table; reproduced when HGP specificity exceeds DELTA specificity under (a); (b), the printed counts 5/5 against 1/5, is reported; blocked if the readings disagree on which is more specific.

In [26]:
rows = []
for z, w, kind, dl, hg, ok in list(readings(amys=soz_mask)) + [("Table 2 printed", "", "paper", paper_delta, paper_hgp, True)]:
    if not ok:
        rows.append({"z": z, "window": w, "kind": kind, "defined": ok})
        continue
    sh, sd = int((hg[soz_mask] <= 0).sum()), int((dl[soz_mask] >= 0).sum())
    table = np.array([[sh, 7 - sh], [sd, 7 - sd]])
    p = stats.chi2_contingency(table, correction=False)[1] if (table.sum(0) > 0).all() else np.nan
    rows.append({"z": z, "window": w, "kind": kind, "defined": ok, "HGP_specific": f"{sh}/7", "DELTA_specific": f"{sd}/7",
                 "which": "HGP" if sh > sd else "DELTA" if sd > sh else "tie", "p_chi2": p})
rf = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(rf.round(3).to_string(index=False))
pb = stats.chi2_contingency(np.array([[5, 0], [1, 4]]), correction=False)[1]
pby = stats.chi2_contingency(np.array([[5, 0], [1, 4]]), correction=True)[1]
print(f"Reading (b), the printed counts 5/5 against 1/5: chi-square p = {pb:.4f} (with Yates' correction {pby:.4f}); paper p ~ 0.2")
c = counted(rf)
print("Counted readings:", len(c), "; more specific:", c.which.value_counts().to_dict())

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The readings disagree on which response is more specific. With window c, the only window that defines the MIs of all 7 SOZ amygdalae, HGP is more specific under baseline (5/7 against 2/7, chi-square p = 0.11) and amygdala (7/7 against 1/7, p = 0.001), and the two are tied under trial (3/7 each). The variants also give HGP (6/7 against 1/7 and 3/7). Under reading (b), the printed counts, HGP is more specific with p = 0.0098 (0.053 with Yates' correction), not about 0.2; no reading gives a p near 0.2.

This outcome rests on an assumption: window (c), fixed windows taken from the Results' text, is the only window that defines the MIs it needs, while the paper defines the MI over the interval where the two curves are significantly separated (Table 2 legend). The question is for the authors (methods_unavailable).

neuron-count¶

Spike sorting gave 50 putative neuron clusters from 9 amygdalae, of which 41 had a firing rate above 1 Hz and were analysed.

fig3a-firing-increase-aversive¶

All 41 neurons fire more during AVERSIVE than during NEUTRAL sequences (FRV 0.26 plus or minus 0.15).

Criterion: FRV (AVERSIVE minus NEUTRAL mean rate) over (a) the 24 s blocks or (b) the 26 s trials; reproduced when every neuron has FRV > 0 and the mean is within 0.15 of 0.26 under one reading; partially reproduced when the mean is within tolerance and most neurons have FRV > 0.

fig3a-firing-gradual-sustained¶

The neurons' firing rose gradually and stayed enhanced throughout the AVERSIVE sequences, not as an immediate response at onset.

Criterion: population AVERSIVE minus NEUTRAL rate (100 ms bins, 1 s smoothing), (a) the difference over 0 to 2 s smaller than over 2 to 24 s and positive in each of the twelve 2 s bins; (b) its first peak later than 2 s and positive to 24 s; reproduced when both hold, not reproduced when both fail.

fig3b-firing-hgp-no-condition-difference¶

Across neurons, the correlation of firing rate with macro-electrode HGP does not differ between the AVERSIVE and NEUTRAL conditions.

A claim of absence: Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the per-neuron Spearman r (AVERSIVE against NEUTRAL) at p < 0.05. HGP is the Methods 4.8 envelope of the bipolar channel of the neuron's amygdala, without per-trial normalisation (a Spearman r within one block is unchanged by any per-trial normalisation). The claims file's readings: time bases (a) 1 s, (b) 1.5 s with 5 points, (c) 15 s; spans (i) the condition's blocks laid end to end, (ii) per block and averaged. In (i) each block is smoothed (or binned into 1.5 s bins) on its own before the blocks are laid end to end, so that no sample of a condition's series carries the other condition or a baseline clip. A variant, concat_session, smooths over the whole session first (the first revision's form), to show what that mixing does.

Result: partially reproduced. The readings of the claims file disagree. Per block and averaged, no time base finds a difference (p 0.72 to 0.83), and neither does the 1 s time base over the blocks laid end to end (r = 0.085 +- 0.130 in AVERSIVE and 0.094 +- 0.124 in NEUTRAL, p = 0.54). Over the blocks laid end to end on the 1.5 s and 15 s time bases, each block smoothed on its own, the test finds NEUTRAL higher (p = 0.012 and 0.023, median differences -0.087 and -0.131). So the claimed absence holds in 4 of the 6 readings. Smoothing over the whole session before selecting the blocks (variant concat_session) gives p = 0.002 and 0.009 for those two, so the mixing of neighbouring blocks strengthened the difference but does not explain it. The means are within the stated spreads under every reading.

The outcome is partially reproduced, not blocked: the six readings are named by the claims file, so no method detail is left to choose; the test was run under each, and the claimed absence holds under some and fails under others, that is, it holds only in part. Unlike the criteria of fig1b-delta-decrease and fig1f-hgp-more-specific-than-delta, this criterion does not say to block when its readings disagree.

fig3c-ssi-frv-correlation¶

Across neurons, the spatial synchronization index (SSI) is strongly positively correlated with the firing rate variability (FRV).

SSI per neuron is the mean Spearman correlation of its firing rate with each neuron of the same amygdala on a different microwire (Methods 4.11, "neighboring neurons recorded in the same amygdala but on different microwires"). The units table is printed first, to see whether it records the microwire. Where it does not, every other unit of the amygdala is used, an assumption (the Results say "all neighboring neurons"), and a variant drops the pairs that are likely on one wire by a spike train test: units sorted from one microwire cannot both be detected within about 1 ms of each other, so a pair with no spikes within +-1 ms where the flanks (2 to 12 ms) predict at least 3 is taken to share a wire. Time bases (a) 100 ms smoothed over 1 s, (b) 15 s, over the whole session (the epochs both units were recorded in). FRV over the blocks.

Result: not reproduced (resting on an assumption). The units table records no microwire: each unit points only to the bipolar macro channel of its amygdala, and the file holds one electrode group. SSI therefore uses every other unit of the amygdala (the assumption). The spike train test finds 4 of 116 testable pairs likely on one wire; the other pairs fire within 1 ms of each other about as often as the flanks predict (median ratio 1.19). SSI and FRV are positively correlated, but weakly: r = 0.26 (p = 0.11) on the 1 s time base and r = 0.40 (p = 0.009) on the 15 s one, over the 41 units with another unit in their amygdala, against r = 0.78, p < 1e-7. Dropping the 4 pairs gives 0.24 (p = 0.13) and 0.35 (p = 0.023). The criterion needs p < 0.05 under every reading for a partial result.

fig3d-firing-correlations-modalities (HGP part)¶

Across neurons, the ongoing firing rate correlates positively with muHGP (0.27), HGP (0.19) and BOLD (0.23), and the correlation is lowest with HGP.

Per neuron, Spearman r of firing rate with the HGP envelope of its amygdala over the session (observed epochs, baseline clips included), (a) 15 s smoothing (Fig. 3D legend), (b) 1.5 s bins smoothed over 5 points (Methods 4.10). muHGP and BOLD are not in the dandiset, so the means for them and the two Wilcoxon tests cannot be computed.

fig4b-regression-firing-hgp¶

The per-neuron correlation of firing rate with HGP is described by both FRV and SSI in a multiple linear regression.

Dependent variable the per-neuron firing-HGP r (fig3d readings), independent FRV and SSI (fig3c readings, same time base where both exist). r read as (a) the multiple correlation R, (b) Spearman r of fitted against observed. Units with an SSI only.

Result: not reproduced (resting on an assumption). The regression describes the firing-HGP correlation: R = 0.56 to 0.68 over the four time-base readings, with model p from 6e-6 to 7e-4; on the 15 s time bases R = 0.635 (within 0.059 of 0.59) with model p = 5.6e-5. But SSI carries it alone (p <= 2e-4 in every reading) and FRV does not (p 0.07 to 0.65, coefficient negative in three readings), so "described by both FRV and SSI", the claim and the criterion's condition, fails in every reading. Dropping the pairs likely on one wire from SSI changes none of this. The SSI rests on the assumption of fig3c-ssi-frv-correlation.

Claims not tested here¶

  • fig3b-firing-muhgp-higher-aversive: needs the continuous microwire signals; the dandiset holds only spike times and mean waveforms of the microwire data (as the data descriptor says).
  • fig2-participant4-bold-correlations, table2-bold-correlations-group, table2-bold-correlation-values, bold-hgp-uncorrelated-low-mi, fig4c-regression-firing-bold, fig4d-hgp-bold-covariation: need the BOLD time courses of the clinical fMRI, which the paper names no public deposit for; the dandiset holds no fMRI.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The paper links no code. Where its Methods leave a step open, every reading named in the claims file was run, and the outcomes are judged on all of them; fixed MI windows taken from the Results' text were run as a further reading, and two z-scoring variants (trialsd, baselinepool) and the two other baselines of Methods 4.8 are shown without deciding any outcome. The z-scoring decides most iEEG outcomes: z-scoring over the whole trial removes the sustained delta decrease, while z-scoring against the baseline keeps it. The paper's MI window, the group clusters, does not exist for HGP here, so the claims on the HGP MI rest on the fixed windows, an assumption. The group test is a within-patient form of the paper's mixed model, which gives the same condition estimate for this balanced design (t differs slightly). SSI uses every other unit of the amygdala, as the dandiset does not say which microwire a unit was on. Epochs in which a unit has no spike at all are taken as not recorded.

What was found about the dandiset. Each session is deposited twice with identical data. The iEEG is stated in volts but holds microvolts. The 26 s epochs are laid end to end with jumps at their boundaries, and the trial table puts the first trial's start at its baseline and the others' at block onset. The units' observation intervals cover all 17 epochs although the 16 units of subject 7 have no spikes after 286 s and four units of subject 2 none in the first epoch. Two ages differ from the paper (subject 2's file gives 39, the age of the paper's patient 7), five channel locations name the hippocampus or are unknown for channels the paper places in the amygdala, no unit is assigned to a microwire, and the units are in 8 amygdalae of 5 patients, not the 9 amygdalae of the Results nor the amygdalae of Table 1 (subject 7 has units, 5 and 8 none). Re-mapping subjects 2 and 7, or 7 to the paper's 5 and 8, does not bring the MIs closer to Table 2. The BOLD time courses and the continuous microwire signals are not in the dandiset.
